A study on the burden and etiologies of acute febrile illnesses (AFI) in Kenya reported an increase in CHIKV cases in Mombasa between December 2017 and December 2019. Using next-generation sequencing on the Illumina MiSeq platform, we established molecular characteristics and phylogenetic differences of the CHIKVs collected from the two epidemiologically distinct settings. These molecular markers provide useful information on CHIKV spread and can help strengthen outbreak preparedness and response. No differences were observed in the frequency of cough, skin rash, conjunctivitis, or vomiting.

title: Limitaciones funcionales y en las actividades de la vida diaria en adultos con antecedente de fiebre Chikungunya en Asunción y Gran Asunción

analysis.research_question_and_background: La fiebre Chikungunya cursa con artralgia que puede persistir más allá de la fase aguda y afectar la funcionalidad. Tras la epidemia registrada en Paraguay, la información local sobre limitaciones funcionales en personas con antecedente de la enfermedad es escasa.
analysis.study_design_and_population: El objetivo fue describir las limitaciones funcionales y en las actividades de la vida diaria en una muestra de adultos con antecedente de fiebre Chikungunya residentes en Asunción y Gran Asunción. Se incluyeron 95 adultos con antecedente autorreferido de fiebre Chikungunya, captados por muestreo no probabilístico por conveniencia mediante un cuestionario digital autoadministrado.
analysis.methods: Se aplicó una adaptación no validada del Health Assessment Questionnaire. El análisis fue descriptivo.
analysis.main_results: La muestra estuvo compuesta mayoritariamente por mujeres (67/95; 70,5 %) y por participantes menores de 30 años (61/95; 64,2 %). La mayoría se encontraba en fase subaguda: 48/95 (50,5 %) habían cursado la infección tres meses antes y 8/95 (8,4 %) seis meses antes o más. Según la clasificación global del instrumento adaptado, el 52,5 % presentó dificultad funcional leve, el 30,7 % moderada y el 16,8 % grave.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: En esta muestra, mayoritariamente en fase subaguda, se observaron limitaciones funcionales frecuentes en la movilidad de miembros inferiores y en la destreza manual.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Los hallazgos pueden informar sobre la necesidad de monitorear las limitaciones funcionales en pacientes con fiebre Chikungunya y considerar su impacto en la calidad de vida.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Los hallazgos no son generalizables y requieren confirmación con estudios de base poblacional y con diagnóstico verificado.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to describe functional limitations and daily activity difficulties in adults with a history of Chikungunya fever in Asunción and Gran Asunción, Paraguay. It was a cross-sectional observational study involving 95 adults with self-reported Chikungunya infection, recruited through non-probabilistic convenience sampling using a digital self-administered questionnaire. The Health Assessment Questionnaire, an unvalidated adaptation, was used to assess functional difficulties. The majority of participants were women and under 30 years old, with most in the subacute phase of the infection. Results showed that 52.5% had mild functional difficulty, 30.7% moderate, and 16.8% severe. The authors concluded that functional limitations, particularly in lower limb mobility and manual dexterity, were common in this subacute phase sample. However, they emphasized that these findings are not generalizable and require confirmation through population-based studies with verified diagnoses. The study's limitations include its non-probabilistic sampling method and lack of validated tools, which may affect the reliability of the results.

title: Antiviral responses of Aedes mosquitoes to Old World alphaviruses.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the antiviral responses of Aedes mosquitoes to Old World alphaviruses, specifically Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), and examines the mechanisms by which these mosquitoes defend against CHIKV infections. The central question is to understand the intrinsic and extrinsic factors that influence vector competence and antiviral defense against CHIKV.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of current knowledge on antiviral defense mechanisms in Aedes mosquitoes against Old World alphaviruses, including CHIKV. It integrates findings from intrinsic immune responses and extrinsic factors such as microbial interactions and Wolbachia infection. The review does not explicitly report on meta-analysis or pooled estimates, but it summarizes existing literature and proposes mechanisms for long-term immune memory.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that RNA interference (RNAi) is the dominant antiviral defense mechanism against alphaviruses, including CHIKV, in Aedes mosquitoes. Canonical immune signaling pathways such as Toll, IMD, JAK/STAT, and JNK show limited or species-specific activity. Additionally, the review highlights the role of piRNAs derived from viral-derived DNA and endogenous viral elements in contributing to long-term immune memory. It also notes that superinfection exclusion and Wolbachia infection are important extrinsic factors that shape vector competence to CHIKV.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies that the mechanisms of antiviral defense against alphaviruses in Aedes mosquitoes are not fully understood, particularly in comparison to the well-characterized responses to orthoflavivirus infections. There is limited evidence on the long-term effects of piRNAs and the role of specific immune pathways in persistent CHIKV infections. The review also notes that the evidence on immune evasion strategies by alphaviruses is still emerging and requires further investigation.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on elucidating the molecular mechanisms of RNAi and canonical immune signaling pathways in Aedes mosquitoes against CHIKV. It also emphasizes the need for studies on the role of piRNAs and extrinsic factors such as Wolbachia infection in shaping vector competence.
